intended_object: The standard Weyl-group representative w_α(1) = x_α(1) x_{-α}(-1) x_α(1) for the long root α = -2e_i in the symplectic group Sp_{2m}(R). This is inferred from the docstring and from the Weyl.lean module.
explanation: In Basic.lean, negativeLongRootTransvectionUnit i c = 1 + c E_{m+i,i} is x_{-2e_i}(c), and positiveLongRootTransvectionUnit i c = 1 + c E_{i,m+i} is x_{2e_i}(c). The definition is x_{-2e_i}(1) · x_{2e_i}(-1) · x_{-2e_i}(1), which is exactly Steinberg's w_α(1) = x_α(1) x_{-α}(-1) x_α(1) for α = -2e_i, as the docstring says. In the (i, m+i) coordinates it multiplies out to the monomial matrix [[0,-1],[1,0]], and the library's lemma coe_negativeLongRootWeylElement identifies it with the elementary Weyl matrix for the pair (m+i, i). It works over any commutative ring. The Fin (m+m) indexing is the library's coordinate model of the symplectic group, and the object is a specific element, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no corresponding Weyl representatives for Chevalley or symplectic groups.
